speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing intense itching and red bumps on your thigh and other areas; tell me, when did these symptoms first start, and have you noticed any new soaps, detergents, or plants since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; given your recent trip to Miami and the nature of the "red bumps," could you describe their appearance (e.g., linear tracks, central punctum, or clusters) and whether you have noticed any mosquito or insect bites? Additionally, have you developed any fever or swollen lymph nodes?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies infestation. The combination of intense itching, red bumps, a recent trip to a conference (close contact), and the distribution on the thigh is highly characteristic. The lack of systemic symptoms like fever further supports a parasitic etiology over an infectious one.
